html:
SMTO-LLM-0082 — SMTO couldn't turn off thinking for its retry

GUID: 29534054-1017-42af-a62b-7d34a1fdd95e
Slug: brain-freeze-thinking-unsupported
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model got stuck, so SMTO tried again with thinking turned off. This model connection wouldn't keep that setting, so SMTO stopped instead of sending the retry. No action from the stuck step ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, open Limits and recovery, turn off Prevent brain freeze, and select Save Main. Your model service can't switch thinking off on request, so this retry method can't work with it.
  2. Or ask the person who runs your model service to support switching thinking off per request, and confirm it works before trying again. With that support in place, SMTO's stuck-step retry can work as designed.
  3. Then select Resume on the stopped task, or start a new task. No action from the stuck step ran, so continuing won't repeat anything.

What success looks like

  • The task continues past the stuck step, or a later stall shows a normal recovery message instead of this one.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your model service. Don't carry out the stuck step's half-written action yourself, and don't keep retrying with the same settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • During a Prevent brain freeze retry, the negotiated request no longer carried chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false (the endpoint had rejected or dropped that control), so SMTO refused to send the retry.

What this means

  • The negotiated retry request could not retain the explicit thinking-off control required by brain-freeze recovery. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The negotiated retry request could not retain the explicit thinking-off control required by brain-freeze recovery.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the negotiated request support for the Thinking switch; distinguish an omitted unsupported control from a provider that later continues reasoning.

How to fix it

  • Use an endpoint whose chat template honours chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking (for example vLLM with a thinking-aware template) and confirm it accepts the control, or turn off Prevent brain freeze under Limits and recovery for the role in Settings › Setup › Model routing. No operation from the rejected decision was executed.
  • Use an endpoint or chat template supporting the Thinking switch, or turn off Prevent brain freeze. No operation from the rejected decision was executed.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Prevent brain freeze: model-configuration / llm_prevent_brain_freeze. Applies to: immediate.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the endpoint supports disabling thinking before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The endpoint accepts and preserves the thinking-off control for the permitted recovery attempt, or the user deliberately disables that recovery feature.

What not to do

  • Do not execute incomplete tool arguments or repeatedly retry the same rejected decision.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
